A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SudoLM research. All main sections, Appendices A–C, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original medical and TOFU access-control experiments, utility evaluations, and key-guessing tests in Tables 1–3, plus model-response examples in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Tables 1–3 and the qualitative model-response study in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same ten-token key design, system-prompt placement, preference-pair construction, and authorization-alignment objectives. No algorithmic or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use medical Chat-Doctor data and TOFU for the same access-control scenarios, generated public queries, and MT-Bench, MMLU, and ARC-Challenge utility benchmarks. No coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same base-model and SFT comparisons and Vanilla/Anchor controls. Appendix C also retains the same comparison involving key placement in the user instruction.

E3.justification: The medical 20% holdout, 1,000 generated public queries, TOFU forget10/retain90 setup, backbone models, metrics, and five-shot MMLU/ARC evaluations are unchanged. Table 3 retains the same key-guessing procedure.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 and Table 3 retain key-guessing tests at lengths 5, 10, and 20. Appendix C/Figure 3 retains the same medical case examining key presence and prompt placement; no analyses are added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten generated keys per length and average refusal rates in Table 3. Neither adds run or seed disclosures, uncertainty intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The result entries and findings in Tables 1–3 and Appendix C are unchanged. For example, Llama3 medical access-control F1 remains 99.83 in Table 2, and all Table 3 key-guessing tests still report 100% refusal.

T1.justification: The access-control definitions in Section 2.1, DPO formulation in Section 2.2, and authorization-alignment equations in Section 3 are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same metric classification; no proofs or derivations are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about credential-dependent knowledge access, preserved general utility, and demonstrations in two application scenarios.

C2.justification: Interpretations of utility preservation, TOFU class imbalance, and key-guessing robustness are unchanged. Both retain the same limitations concerning backbone coverage, fixed keys, binary access levels, and key-leakage risks.

D1.justification: v3 adds a first-page footnote directing readers to the SudoLM GitHub page for code release, which v2 lacks. This adds code-access information; the documented implementation and experimental details otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 and the bibliography retain the same cited works and positioning relative to safety alignment, controllable generation, and beneficial applications of backdooring.

P1.justification: v3 adds a short Acknowledgment section after the conclusion and a code-release footnote. The scientific prose and section sequence otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The additions cause limited column and page reflow, including shifts in the conclusion and references. Figures 1–3 and Tables 1–4 retain their displays and captions; the appendix pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: The new code-release pointer modestly improves reproducibility documentation, and the acknowledgment adds funding transparency. Scientific content and evidence remain unchanged, so the gain is limited. The PDFs alone do not establish the linked code's completeness or usability.
